key_insight: LLM-authored notes can modestly degrade downstream LLM summaries, while unconfirmed diagnoses can reappear in later outputs without detectable changes in standard quality metrics.
clinical_relevance: AI-assisted documentation workflows may need safeguards against accumulated note bloat and propagation of unconfirmed diagnoses.
method: Evaluated seven reader LLMs from four model families.
Compared LLM-generated summary notes with length-matched copy-forward and templated text.
Injected diagnostic overcalls and assessed their reappearance in downstream outputs.
evidence_signal: Across the tested models, LLM-generated notes modestly but consistently degraded hospital-course generation, while overcall propagation rates varied by reader model.
watch_item: Standard quality metrics did not detect changes associated with overcall propagation; the abstract does not establish effects on patient outcomes.
paper_title: AI in the Clinical Documentation Loop: Effects of LLM-Induced Note Bloat and Diagnostic Overcall on Downstream LLMs
